Entertainment.title: Earl and MIKE Drop, Ye Returns to the Stage: Everything We Loved in Music This Week
Entertainment.text: All of the biggest music headlines in one place and playlist. Updated live throughout the week.Ravyn Lenae Reveals New Two-Pack, Equipped With a Dominic Fike FeatureFor her first release of 2026, Ravyn Lenae has doubled down. While her "Love Me Not" was one of the key players in the unofficial 2025 "Song of the Summer" bracket, Lenae is back on the scene just in time for the warm weather once again. She has released a pair of singles dubbed "Bobby" and "Reputation," the latter of which features Dominic Fike. This marks the first-ever in-studio collaboration from the indie-pop, genre-bending pair, and comes accompanied by a cinematic, Matthew Dillon Cohen-directed visual.The Ultimate Yoshi Link-UpAfter retiring Childish Gambino, Donald Glover is fully embracing his new alias of Yoshi. So much so that he took to Dodger Stadium on Tuesday night to throw the first pitch for the Dodgers game against the Cleveland Guardians – and, of course, link up with fellow Yoshi, Yoshinobu Yamamoto.Earl Sweatshirt, MIKE, and SURF GANG's POMPEII//UTILITY Revels in "Unspoken Creative Synergy"“We have a whole counsel situation over here,” Earl Sweatshirt said on Wednesday night’s Stone Island POMPEII // UTILITY in-store listening event. “I think that’s why it works well. We review everything from every single perspective.” This was just one of the gems Earl dropped at the intimate New York City listening party and panel earlier this week. Sat alongside his POMPEII // UTILITY collaborators MIKE and SURF GANG, the trio, in conversation with the Stone Island team and album artist Sharif Farrag, authentically reflected on the creative process of the communally awaited collaborative opus, which is an endeavor MIKE refers to as one that’s rooted in an “unspoken creative synergy.” Hear more from all three contributing parties on the New York City-centric collaborative opus in the full story here.Gap-Chella Loading...If there's one thing about Coachella, the weather will flip like a switch; the days in the desert are sweltering, and the nights are prime hoodie weather. Who better to be on-site serving up limited-release hoodies than the Gap? Announced earlier this week via Instagram, the label continues to align itself closer to the music scene in another big move, hosting what it's calling the "Hoodie House" at the tentpole California festival.A New POMPEII/UTILITY Offering: "Home on the Range"Sharing the same name as the pair's co-headlining tour slate, "Home on the Range," lands as the latest lead track from Earl Sweatshirt and MIKE's SURF GANG-produced collab album, POMPEII/UTLITY. And Another One: "Back Home"With the rollout in full effect, another pre-release single from POMPEII/UTILITY  has materialized shortly after "Home on the Range." Dubbed "Back Home," this one is a byproduct of just MIKE x SURF GANG, appearing on the POMPEII part of the double-disked-up LP.Supreme x DJ ScrewSupreme has been deep in its music bag as of late, fresh off the Juelz Santana shoot and a collaboration with Teenage Engineering, the New York imprint has teamed up with the estate of the legendary DJ Screw for a lineup of apparel and goods. Items include a football jersey, hoodies, tees, and a signature bobblehead.The First BULLY Visual Is a Fever DreamDirected by Bianca Censori, Ye has lifted the veil on the music video for "Father," which marks the first official visual from BULLY, and let's just say – it's a hard one to put into words. Feeling like a literal scene from a textbook fever dream, the Censori-lensed clip is a scene envisioned in a church. A pastor stands at the pulpit and the choir on the side, while the pews are packed with a sea of notable attendees, ranging from Michael Jackson (yes, Michael Jackson), a full police squad, a magician mid-card trick at all times, a knight in shining armor, a cat-faced woman and her child, and a nun in deep slumber. Churchgoers – others, including a chef with a comically large cake and twin brides – walk down the aisle and pause in front of the pastor. A UFO touches down, and Travis Scott and Ye join the scene, suited up, both donning a full-face alien mask, which they then remove to reveal themselves.Stone Island Shows Up To Support Earl Sweatshirt, MIKE, and SURF GANG's POMPEII / UTILITYStone Island has always closely aligned its brand ethos with the music industry, but in the past year, the Italian imprint has doubled down on its affinity for the sonic scene. After a year of successful listening parties and DJ sets and fresh off the heels of a Miami Music Week in-store event with Apple Music, Stone Island has situated itself alongside underground rap, specifically in a capacity that pays tribute to both the old and new guards of the space. Stone Island Sound chose to champion Earl Sweatshirt and MIKE‘s first-ever, highly anticipated, SURF GANG-produced joint album, POMPEII/UTILITY, hosting a series of listening parties – in the brand's flagship stores in Los Angeles, New York City, and London – in tandem with Q&A panels as well as producing a lineup of limited-edition vinyls. Read the full story here.Ye's ReturnAll eyes were on SoFi Stadium on Wednesday night when Ye made his return to the Los Angeles stage. He stepped out onto a planet-shaped set, delivered a career-spanning setlist, and brought out Don Toliver and North West.Fetty Wap Goes Sinners Mode in New VisualAfter dropping off his first post-prison record last Friday, Zavier, Fetty Wap has shared the first music video from the LP. Edgar Esteves brings "White Roses" to life in a Sinners-inspired music video, with Fetty channelling his inner Stack and Smoke. It's clear the musician has returned to the scene with a more focused vision, stepping into new sonic territory and ensuring the visual component is up to par.Jeezy For BIKE AIRFor Nigel Sylvester's latest BIKE AIR range, he's enlisted a fellow legend to front the lookbook: Jeezy. With the Air Jordan 4 as the centerfold of the collection, Jeezy pairs the sneakers with a selection of new apparel as well. “It was an honor to collaborate with Jeezy on the ‘Brick After Brick’ BIKE AIR lookbook at the iconic Brooklyn Banks. I spent a lot of years BMX riding at the Banks, with Jeezy’s music as a constant source of motivation,” Sylvester told Hypebeast in an exclusive quote. “This is a full circle moment for me that emphasizes the Brick After Brick ethos. This is motion, creativity, and consistency coming together to create something timeless.” Read more in the full story here.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Entertainment.title: Maison Margiela Enters Haute Parfumerie With the Scentsorium Collection
Entertainment.text: SummaryMaison Margiela has officially launched The Scentsorium Collection, a luxurious new line of six genderless fragrances releasing this monthTranslating the house's signature couture principles into scent, the collection manipulates and reconstructs raw ingredients to reflect profound human emotionsThe six unique fragrances are housed in striking, asymmetrical flacons designed to resemble repurposed early twentieth-century decanters pierced with a glass splinterMaison Margiela is bringing its iconic, avant-garde couture codes directly into the world of haute parfumerie. Arriving this April, the Parisian fashion house has unveiled The Scentsorium Collection, an ambitious suite of six luxury genderless fragrances. Developed using the rigorous, deconstructive principles of the brand's Artisanal Atelier, the new line meticulously separates, adjusts, and recombines raw ingredients to capture the visceral intensity and complex dualities of human emotion.Developed entirely within the framework of haute parfumerie, the collection treats scent the exact same way the Atelier treats physical garments. Materials are intentionally stripped back to their most essential forms, refined through heat or pressure, and ultimately reconstructed into entirely new, unexpected compositions."The Scentsorium Collection unveils the untamed essence of the very core of human," explained Sandrine Groslier, Global President of Luxe Fragrance Brands. "We meticulously captured the unfabricated truth of our most profound emotions... by applying the rigorous precision of haute couture to raw ingredients. This radical artistry in craftsmanship defines our entry into Haute Parfumerie."To properly showcase the tension between raw materials, the six fragrances are deeply rooted in specific emotional states. Blaze Of Stillness captures the suspense of hope by anchoring clear neroli blossom with dense fig and musky suede. Exploring the push and pull of desire, Anguish and Awe shifts between lightness and weight using concentrated black rose, slow-extracted fruit notes, and a supple suede accord. Meanwhile, Delight in Despair experiments with temperature and texture, blending distilled cypriol root with aromatic saffron cream to evoke a shifting sense of euphoria.On the heavier end of the emotional spectrum, Silent Fury channels anger and sudden release through a restrained but powerful mix of deep leather, dry spices, and smoked tobacco absolute. Tender Defiance embraces pure audacity with an intersection of metallic liquorice, heated incense resin, and smoke. Finally, Fit of Folly emulates the feeling of rapture, utilizing continuous layers of evolving patchouli and clear mineral musk to create a sensation of endless, looping motion.Reflecting Maison Margiela’s deep connection to time and reinterpretation, the packaging itself acts as a standalone work of art. The flacon mimics the aesthetic of an inherited, early twentieth-century decanter that has been repurposed by a contemporary owner. The rectangular cut-glass silhouette features a curved interior chamber and a nipped metal atomizer, heavily defined by a deliberate, striking irregularity: the glass is violently pierced with a splinter that drives a prism directly through the form.The Scentsorium Collection officially launches globally in April 2026, offering a radical new sensory experience for a discerning generation of luxury fragrance connoisseurs.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Entertainment.title: The Crossover: Where Golf Shows Up Beyond the Fairway
Entertainment.text: Golf’s cultural shift isn’t happening all at once, it’s unfolding through a series of smaller, intentional crossovers. What was once a sport defined by tradition is now increasingly shaped by adjacent worlds. Basketball doesn’t stay on the court, football doesn’t stay on the pitch and hospitality isn’t just service. Golf, for the first time in a long time, is letting all of that in.The shift isn’t about making golf cool. It’s about recognizing that the people shaping culture are already touching the game, just not always through traditional entry points.Jordan Brand partnering with LA golf community SwangJordan linking with Swang isn’t about just entering golf, it’s about choosing where it shows up. Swang sits closer to street culture than traditional golf, built through informal meetups, music and a rejection of the sport’s usual codes. This is about Jordan extending a legitimate “we see you” to the people already reshaping the game. The real shift is that golf’s momentum is coming from smaller, culturally grounded communities.New York Knicks renew collaboration with MalbonThe Knicks x Malbon collab is the clearest sign yet that golf is being swallowed by “lifestyle.” When you can wear a Knicks-branded hoodie or varsity jacket at the muni and then straight to a game at the Garden, the sport stops feeling isolated. It becomes just another layer of how you dress. You don’t need to know how to hit a draw to buy in, the appeal is in the vibe and there's no handicap requirement.Rao’s announces summer residency at Marine & Lawn’s St Andrews hotel View this post on Instagram A post shared by Marine & Lawn Hotels & Resorts (@marineandlawn)Putting Rao’s at Rusacks St Andrews is unexpected, but it says a lot about where golf is headed. Pairing something as rooted as St Andrews with a place like Rao’s shifts “prestige” from history to something more lived-in and urban. The trip isn’t only about playing 18 in the wind, it’s about everything surrounding it. The food, the crowd, the energy after the round. Golf’s still the reason you go, but it’s no longer the only part of the itinerary.adidas Golf drops golf range with Premier League clubs Arsenal and Aston Villa View this post on Instagram A post shared by Aston Villa (@avfcofficial)adidas dropping Premier League clubs like Arsenal and Aston Villa onto the fairway feels inevitable. When you see those club colors on a golf polo, the game suddenly stops looking like a private club and starts looking like a jersey you already own. Even if you don't play golf in it, you’ll wear it and that’s enough to bring golf closer into everyday culture.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Entertainment.title: Earl Sweatshirt, MIKE, and SURF GANG's 'POMPEII//UTILITY' Revels in "Unspoken Creative Synergy"
Entertainment.text: "We have a whole counsel situation over here," Earl Sweatshirt said on Wednesday night's Stone Island POMPEII // UTILITY in-store listening event. "I think that’s why it works well. We review everything from every single perspective."This was just one of the gems Earl dropped at the intimate New York City listening party and panel earlier this week. Sat alongside his POMPEII // UTILITY collaborators MIKE and SURF GANG, the trio, in conversation with the Stone Island team and album artist Sharif Farrag, authentically reflected on the creative process of the communally awaited collaborative opus, which is an endeavor MIKE refers to as one that's rooted in an "unspoken creative synergy.""I think we all traded methods on this project," Sweatshirt expounded on that sentiment. "We all came to the table of Ableton, here ... Working with MIKE and SURF GANG on this project, I learned how to simplify my process. I learned how to play nice with others. I learned how to do that. I learned how to make beats with n*ggas. I thought I knew that before, but I didn’t know how to do that before. I learned how to do that with the gang.”The project is split into two discs, with the first, POMPEII – thematically rooted in destruction and its aftermath – handled entirely by MIKE, and the second, more practical portion, UTILITY, handled by Earl. Totalling 33 tracks from front to back, it's the SURF GANG production that strings each song to its predecessor and its successor, the collective's Harrison actually being the one who pushed for the project's materialization.After teaming up with Earl for "Making the Band (Danity Kane)," the pair pivoted to POMPEII // UTILITY, unknowingly. “All of the conversations in those moments were anticlimactic," reflects Earl on the early stages of deciding to drop a joint album. "It was really just like, 'Yo, you trying to put out a project?' and we were all like 'Yeah,'"“The only thing that was different," he continued, "was that I didn't open any of the beats and listen to them unless I knew I was about to follow through. I cared about all of these beats, so I didn’t want to play them out until they got bland.” He also noted that "each one of the tracks has been [his] favorite at a different point in time."evilgiane spoke about the role New York City played in shaping the SURF GANG superproducer collective's sound, and how that, too, translated heavily into the project. "I grew up listening to all kinds of hip hop – the fried shit, the heavy-bass shit, extra hood shit. My mom told me to keep an open mind," he began. "Every time a rapper and a subgenre of music comes from New York, and that keeps me inspired and not doing the same thing over and over.”POMPEII // UTILITY is a perfect example of the collective's aversion to repetition, taking the form of a true tapestry of different hip-hop, ambient, and alternative influences. Building on the boundless sonic inspiration, the creative process then fell into place naturally as a result."We were both working on SURF GANG beats at the same time, so we wanted to just keep that going," explained Earl. "We were making beats from scratch until like ridiculous hours," added MIKE.Why? "Because it was all about capturing these moments and getting the most out of them," continued Earl. "Harrison has a folder of infinity beats. It’s literally called ‘Good Beats,’ and there’s just a lot of good beats in there. It’s a consistent process, but it’s about capturing the moment. This project is an honest depiction of the moment.” That’s why n*ggas say cooking, I guess. You got some shit going and then if you get distracted, the consistency of it changes, and your perspective on it changes. The moment is gone. And you're about to serve some terrible food.”While it's all about this unspoken, yet instantly palpable, creative synergy, it's also about the come-up. MIKE spent a lot of time on Wednesday night's panel recounting his trajectory, grateful that he's been able to achieve all of this while still standing alongside the people he started up with. The project features a stacked slate of 10k and SURF GANG affiliate artists on the assists, including Niontay, Anysia Kym, Jadasea, Na-Kel Smith and Lerado Khalil."I have this joke that when I’m 45, I’m gonna do a residency at Cafe Erzulie," MIKE closed out the panel with. "That’s where we was at.”We'll be the first in line for presale with the pre-sale tickets drop. Until then, we'll be running up POMPEII // UTILITY, out on all streaming services now.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Entertainment.title: What's in Lebron, Future & Jackson Wang's Bags? Louis Vuitton Will Show You.
Entertainment.text: SummaryPharrell’s "In My Bag" campaign features stars like LeBron James and Jeremy Allen White showcasing their butter-soft, double-tanned calfskin Speedy P9 bags.Highlighting the 1930s icon's modern evolution, the colorful range contains curated essentials—from Future’s tennis racquet to Wembanyama’s alien charms—reflecting the diverse lifestyles of Louis Vuitton’s global ambassadors.Shot by Thomas Lagrange, Louis Vuitton enlisted male ambassadors and Friends of the House to show what they carry in their Speedy P9 bags for its "In My Bag" campaign. In a range of calfskin colorways, the medium-sized carry-all is shown in all its versatility through the distinct lifestyles of Jeremy Allen White, Jude Bellingham, Future, LeBron James, Jackson Wang, and Victor Wembanyama.House Ambassador and Hollywood actor Jeremy Allen White has a fitting curation for his alternative aesthetic. In his green Speedy P9, The Bear star has a copy of the daily newspaper, a spiral-bound notebook, a cap, a comb, a watch, and a charging cord. For basketball legend and multi-time NBA champion LeBron James, the yellow Speedy P9 reveals LeBron's favorite pastimes and grooming essentials, like shaving cream and his signature cap.Fellow basketball player and House Ambassador Victor Wembanyama has an aquatic teal variant of the bag, complete with a Monogram alien charm, containing a deck of cards and wired headphones. Following his Men's SS24 Collection, Pharrell put his signature on the new iteration by adding "P9", named after Paris's Pont-Neuf, where his debut was staged. Entertainment.title: Marcus Allen Breaks Down His Career Journey Through Timepieces with Watches of Switzerland
Entertainment.text: Passionate watch collectors know that timepieces are a symbol of achievement or a commemoration of a significant moment in life. In the same way that vintage clothing tells an elaborate story, every watch is a motif that stands for something bigger. Style connoisseur Marcus Allen has been a collector for years, pouring his verve for storytelling into his clothing and accessory curation process.Allen founded The Society Archive in 2020, though he started the label over a decade prior. Allen and his team began accumulating pieces marked by precise craftsmanship, building a strong archive that highlights attention to detail. As a result, the team also built a close-knit community. When Allen isn’t putting work in with The Society Archive, you can find him creating vintage menswear content or working as a multifaceted creative director. ​​View this post on Instagram A post shared by Hypebeast @Hypebeast As an avid collector, Allen has a trained eye when it comes to picking out meaningful milestone pieces. “I started this archive in high school and have been collecting pieces ever since,” he expressed. “There’s an unspoken language about what we put on our bodies — whether it’s a timepiece or a great leather shoe — these decisions can put you in any place you want to be, socially.” Bringing us along, he walked us through his covetable collection of both fashion grails and watches with Watches of Switzerland, elaborating on special items that signify the ups and downs of his career journey.First, Allen presents the Watches of Switzerland OMEGA Seamaster Planet Ocean 600M, designating this model as a reflection of his early career. The piece honors OMEGA’s dive watch heritage and is powered by a 9900 calibre movement. Designed for use underwater, it shows off Super-LumiNova coated indexes for visibility and a durable stainless steel case.“I feel like this watch is a piece I would have selected at the start of my career because it has much more presence and weight than other timepieces,” Allen shared. “It’s a much bolder model with the blue colorway, and I was just kind of YOLO-ing when I started my career and being very spontaneous. I feel like the Seamaster speaks to that.”Next, the creative pulled out the Watches of Switzerland Vintage and Pre-Owned Cartier Tank Basculante Mécanique – 150th Anniversary Limited Edition, labeling it as a marker of his current career era. The Cartier Tank is a classic model for the brand, but this one comes with its own distinct flair. It’s elevated by a guilloché dial and unique reversible case — and it’s limited to 150 pieces worldwide, making it a very rare find. “Every day I wear a Cartier watch — but this one is special. It’s super low profile as well, but when you see it, you know. It reflects where I’m currently at, since it’s much more refined and low profile, yet still versatile.”Lastly, Allen describes the Watches of Switzerland Vintage and Pre-Owned Patek Philippe Calatrava as his dream piece. The round watch with pure, clean lines is regarded as the quintessential wristwatch in the collector’s universe. It launched in 1932, and though many complications have been added since then, the piece remains timeless.“This felt like an ideal aspirational piece because it feels so grown,” the creative reflected. “It’s very understated from afar, but if you know what you’re looking at, it has connotations of success. I hope I’ll think that highly of myself in 20 years. The piece itself feels very solid as well, and I hope in the future I will have reached a point where I feel that I’ve accomplished all of the things I wanted.”On his future trajectory, Allen shared, “I’m working on a collection currently. I just hope to keep continuing to build upon what we have so far.” As a dedicated collector with a keen eye, Allen’s archive of both watches and rare fashion finds is sure to continue growing, mirroring his blossoming career.Check out Allen’s exclusive vintage clothing and watch collection in the video above. You can browse for your dream watch models at watchesofswitzerland.com.Read more at Hypebeast

                Abstract
                The physical and social exposome affects human aging, and brain clocks may track its effects. However, most studies neglect multidomain exposures (physical, social and political) across diverse settings globally and their associations with brain aging. In this study, we characterized the associations between 73 country-level physical and social exposomal factors and multimodal brain age in 18,701 participants from 34 countries (healthy individuals and those with Alzheimer's disease, frontotemporal lobar degeneration or mild cognitive impairment). Exposome effects were assessed using generalized additive models and meta-analytic frameworks. Aggregated exposome models explained up to 15.5-fold more variance than individual exposures (delta Akaike information criterion (ΔAIC): 2,034-3,127). Physical exposome was primarily associated with accelerated structural brain aging (limbic, subcortical and cerebellar regions), whereas social exposome was more strongly associated with functional brain aging (frontotemporal and limbic networks). Exposome burden accounted for 3.3-9.1-fold higher risk of accelerated aging, exceeding effects of clinical diagnoses. Findings were out-of-sample validated in cross-sectional and longitudinal designs, remained consistent across clinical subgroups and persisted after adjustment for demographics, age correction bias, cognition, scanner type and data quality. The exposome accelerates brain aging in health and disease, underscoring the need to address physical, social and political inequities.
                
                Longevity Relevance Analysis
                The exposome significantly accelerates brain aging in both healthy individuals and those with neurodegenerative diseases. This paper is relevant as it addresses the multifaceted influences on brain aging, highlighting the importance of environmental and social factors in the aging process, which aligns with the broader goals of longevity research.

Longevity & Anti-Aging.title: Imaging-derived biological age across multiple organs links to mortality and aging-related health outcomes.
Longevity & Anti-Aging.text:
Paper Details
                Authors: Veronika Ecker, Bin Yang, Sergios Gatidis, Thomas Küstner
                Institution: Institute of Signal Processing and System Theory, University of Stuttgart, Stuttgart, Germany. veronika.ecker@iss.uni-stuttgart.de.
                
                Journal: npj aging
                
                Abstract
                Aging is a complex, multifactorial process, influencing disease risk and overall health. While chronological age (CA) is widely used in clinical practice, it fails to capture individual aging trajectories. Current approaches to estimate biological age (BA) often focus on single organs or predefined clinical biomarkers, limiting comprehensive assessment. We introduce a novel, purely imaging-driven deep learning framework for organ-specific BA estimation across seven organ systems. Our uncertainty-aware ResNet-based models autonomously learned aging-related features from imaging data in 70,000 UK Biobank participants, eliminating manual feature selection biases. Training on a healthy cohort, where CA approximates BA, allows learning normative aging patterns. When applied to a broader cohort, deviations from typical aging indicate older or younger BA. Our findings demonstrate the feasibility of BA estimation, even in organs with subtle aging features. While aging is largely heterogeneous across organs, we also identified correlations in aging patterns. We further showed that accelerated aging is prognostic of mortality and health outcomes, offering insights for personalized assessments.
                
                Longevity Relevance Analysis
                The paper claims that a novel imaging-driven framework can estimate biological age across multiple organs and its correlation with mortality and health outcomes. This research is relevant as it addresses biological aging, offering insights into personalized assessments and potential interventions in the aging process.
